thread_text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: production-error - multiple 500s observed on /v1/generate starting at 1769600123. Affected region: us-west-2. Service: inference-api. Severity: P1. Paging oncall.
jamal (oncall): I'm on it. pulling logs now. Any customer-facing alerts sent?
incident-bot: No customer alert created yet. Metric spike: token_processing_latency > 2s and 500 rate at 4% for last 2m. Canary deployment ID: canary-2026-03-15-09.
jamal (oncall): Reached dev-runtime oncall: @maria can you confirm if any canary rollout happened ~09:00?
maria (eng-runtime): yes that's canary-2026-03-15-09, rolled 10% to canary pool around 09:02. I see failed DB migration job linked to release: migration job stuck at step "add_index_user_requests" with timeout and deadlocks. Logs:
```
ERROR: relation "user_requests" does not contain column "request_hash_v2"
CONTEXT: SQL statement "CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_user_requests_hash_v2 ON user_requests (request_hash_v2)"
DETAIL: could not open relation mapping for relation 12567
```
maria (eng-runtime): Looks like migration tried to create index on a column that doesn't exist in that replica's schema (backwards-incompatible migration). Might be an ordering problem in deploy.
kevin (db): I'm seeing schema drift between primary and read-replicas. Replication lag ~120s on replica db-rw-07. The migration ran non-atomically and left index creation queued on replica causing DDL lock storms. Killing migration might be safest.
jamal (oncall): Impact: 500s on /v1/generate for canary traffic only? Or global?
maria (eng-runtime): Canary traffic only so far, but routing fallback sent requests to main pool and some requests hit older model variant that depends on new column—hence 500s for certain tenant ids. Product impact limited to 10% of traffic but includes a handful of larger customers. Sophie can you confirm affected customers?
sophie (product): I see three accounts with elevated errors: acme-inc, beacon-ops, fluxio. Notified account leads with temporary notice. Customer success standing by.
alex (eng-sre): Immediate mitigation options: 1) kill the canary feature flag to stop rollout, 2) rollback release, 3) kill migration jobs on replicas, 4) temporarily route canary traffic back to stable model. Prefer kill-flag + rollback if migration is irrecoverable.
jamal (oncall): @maria, can we flip the canary flag quickly? Is there a kill-switch button in console?
maria (eng-runtime): Yes: `POST /admin/flags/canary-2026-03-15-09/disable` or via Console -> Rollouts -> canary-2026-03-15-09 -> Disable. I'll disable now.
maria (eng-runtime): Disabled canary; confirming traffic shift. Deploy-bot: executed route-update to stable pool at 1769600201.
deploy-bot: Route update: canary-2026-03-15-09 -> disabled. Traffic rerouted to stable pool. Status: OK.
jamal (oncall): Monitoring errors and latency. Error rate dropping to 0.8% in the next minute. Good sign.
kevin (db): I'll kill the stuck migration processes on replicas and cancel pending index job. Commands I'm running:
```
-- list blocking queries
SELECT pid, state, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE query LIKE '%CREATE INDEX%';
-- cancel
SELECT pg_cancel_backend(pid);
```
kevin (db): Cancelled long-running DDL on db-rw-07 and db-rw-09. Restarting replica apply worker to clear mapping cache.
kevin (db): Replica apply restarted, replication lag falling to 20s. No new DDL queued.
maria (eng-runtime): Since we disabled canary, can we rollback the release to avoid re-triggering the migration? What's the safest order: rollback code, then run corrective migration on primary, then reupgrade replicas?
alex (eng-sre): Plan A (preferred): rollback code to stable commit (deploy-bot rollback), confirm no new DB DDL will run. Then schedule a controlled migration window: create migration that is backwards-compatible (add column with NULL default, populate, then create index), run on primary, let replicas catch up, then re-deploy. Plan B (if rollback fails): keep canary off and run surgical fix manually on replicas + primary.
jamal (oncall): Sophie / customer comms: advise customers short degradation for 15-30m, we're rolling back the canary, issuing status update.
sophie (product): Sending status message to affected accounts and status.redwood.ai: "We detected elevated errors for some requests following a canary deploy. Canary has been disabled and traffic routed to stable. Engineers are rolling back the release and investigating a DB migration issue. We expect reduced errors within 30 minutes."
deploy-bot: Initiating rollback to commit abc123-stable at 1769600265.
deploy-bot: Rollback started; deleting canary instances and restoring previous model variants.
jamal (oncall): Observability: token latency and 500s back down to baseline. Customer error counts trending down. Marking incident as mitigated but continuing investigation.
kevin (db): Root cause: migration ordering bug in deploy pipeline. Migration job sometimes executed before new code that adds column had been applied on certain replica subsets due to parallel rollout steps. Also migration used non-idempotent DDL (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on non-existent column). Fix: change migration to add column with IF NOT EXISTS, backfill in batches, then index using safer locking strategy.
maria (eng-runtime): Created PR with deploy pipeline guard: ensure schema migration fence is successful across primaries before proceeding to make code changes live. Also adding a pre-deploy check: verify column exists on all writer primaries.
alex (eng-sre): Postmortem action items:
- Database: kevin to produce migration best-practices doc and automated pre-checks (owner: kevin)
- Runtime: maria to add rollout gating for migrations + kill-switch monitoring (owner: maria)
- SRE: jamal to add runbook for canary migration failures and quick rollback steps (owner: jamal)
- Product/CS: sophie to refine customer messaging templates for migration-related rollouts (owner: sophie)
- Deploy: add CI check to reject migrations with unsafe DDL (owner: eng-platform)
kevin (db): I'll run a safe remediation migration in maintenance window tonight: add column IF NOT EXISTS, backfill in small batches, create index after verification. No blocking expected.
jamal (oncall): Closing the pager. Marking incident resolved at 1769600360. Please file a postmortem and link here.
sophie (product): Filing a customer follow-up note. Thanks all for fast response. :white_check_mark:
maria (eng-runtime): Follow-up: I'll add a dashboard to alert on DDL errors during rollouts and surface migration status in the Console. :hammer_and_wrench:
alex (eng-sre): Good coordination. We'll sync tomorrow for RCA and preventive changes.
